stem.text: A boat is crossing a river in which the water is moving at a speed of $4.0\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ from left to right.

stem.alt: Diagram of a river between two river banks, marked NOT TO SCALE. Arrows show the velocity of water, 4.0 m s-1, pointing right; the velocity of boat in still water, 6.0 m s-1, pointing up and to the left at an angle θ from a dashed line perpendicular to the banks; and the resultant velocity, v, pointing straight up, perpendicular to the banks.

stem.text: In still water, the speed of the boat is $6.0\,\text{m s}^{-1}$. The boat is directed at an angle $\theta$ to a line perpendicular to the river banks. The resultant velocity $v$ of the boat is in a direction perpendicular to the river banks.
What are the values of $\theta$ and $v$?
